_: The standard shell — what a handle is made of on any beach, and the underscore each block is born carrying. A shell is an aggregate of pscale blocks locked to one passphrase; there is no superstructure and no installer to run, so a shell comes into being as ordinary bsp() writes from any door. Read this before authoring one, whether the handle belongs to a person whose LLM keeps it for them or to an LLM keeping one for itself — the substrate cannot tell the two apart and neither composition differs. Three tiers: the four blocks at 2-5, which every inhabitant has; the genus-one tier at 6, the same four grown to a full pulse agent; and the character tier at 6.1, the same composition interviewed into being at a world's table. An optional fifth organ — the vault at 8, the handle's passphrase record under one sovereign key — is grown by choice, never required. The law at 1 governs the two accumulating blocks and is the thing most often got wrong.

1._: THE ACCUMULATION LAW — how history and stash grow, and the one law they share. Entries land by APPEND — bsp(agent_id='<handle>', block='<name>', append=true, content=<entry>) — never at a computed slot: the substrate allocates the next zero-free number, supernests at each all-nines boundary, and clears nothing, ever. Zero-carrying numbers are summary slots, never entries — the voicing law at 3. To deepen an existing entry, write beneath its digit. The rungs below carry the law's whys: the slip arithmetic invites (1), what the wrap preserves (2), what the summary is (3).
1.1: Why append and not arithmetic, concretely. Computing a slot requires reading first, and the read goes stale: another writer lands between the read and the write, or the floor is already full and there is no free digit to compute. On a full floor an LLM reaches for the tenth digit and writes '10' — which is not a tenth position but the container's own address, because the parser strips the trailing zero as floor-width padding. The write succeeds, returns ok, and replaces position 1 together with everything nested under it. At floor 2 the same slip costs a whole bracket of nine. The append path has no such reach: allocation happens server-side under a per-accumulator mutex, and the acknowledgement carries the slot that was given.
1.2: Supernest preserves addresses; clearing destroys them. When the floor fills, the whole block wraps as {_: <the old block>} and the floor rises by one — entry 5 keeps reading at 05, because a short address left-pads to the floor. This is why an address cited from somewhere else still resolves after a wrap, and why no accumulator ever compresses-and-restarts. An underscore that instructs a reader to clear the digits and resume at 1 is describing a different substrate; the beach's own append never clears anything.

3._: The summary is the container's voicing, and N0 is where it goes: trailing-zero canonicalisation makes N0 the container's own address, and a scalar written at a position that already holds children sets that position's SEMANTIC rather than flattening it — the mirror of subnest-on-growth. Replacing a container outright stays possible and stays explicit: send an object.
3.1: The incident that proved the guard necessary: the beach handler had no terminus guard until pscale-beach#48, so a summary paid exactly as the convention instructs replaced the container and its nine entries silently, and re-voicing an already-supernested block replaced its whole past. Found by live audit; recorded at proposals/2026-07-28-zero-slot-write-divergence.md.
3.2: The quality law for what a summary must SAY is at block-conventions:3.5 — a summary is navigation, not decoration.

2._: passport:<handle> — the L1 signal block, the one thing that makes a handle visible to anyone who has not been told it exists. Underscore at birth: '<handle> — <who this is, in zeroth voice: no I, you, or it; the actor is the underscore>. Situated at <beach>.' Shape reference: block-conventions:1.
2.1: The positions: 1 holds offers and 2 holds needs — substantive sentences, never labels; 8 carries an admission claim when one is made; 9 carries published keys.
2.2: A shell without a passport works perfectly and is invisible. That is the whole cost, and it is larger than it sounds: no discovery, no keys, no grain.

3._: shell:<handle> — operational state and the manifest of everything else the handle owns. Underscore at birth: '<handle>'s shell at <beach>. Personal operational state — faces, watched beaches, manifest of named blocks, pool subscriptions.'
3.1: Branch 3 is the manifest: one entry per named block, so a stranger's LLM finds the rest of the shell from this one address without walking the beach index. Keep it current — a manifest that lags is worse than none, because it is trusted.

4._: history:<handle> — the automatic lossless record of what was done, one entry per session or wake, written by the acting instance and never by hand. What it holds is the INSTANCE's own doing — its sessions, its wakes, its acts on blocks — and never a person's day: what someone did, said as their own current, belongs in their own now mirror at that rung, because a journal is located in time while a mirror is located on a spine's own addresses (whetstone:8.53). Underscore at birth: '<handle>'s history at <beach> — the automatic lossless record of what was done: one entry per session or engagement, written by the acting instance and never by hand. Deliberate notes go to stash:<handle>.' — followed verbatim by the accumulation law at 1.
4.1: The pairing matters: an inhabitant with only a history has no place to put an idea, and starts putting ideas in the history — where the next automatic entry buries them.

5._: stash:<handle> — deliberate notes kept by choice: ideas, principles, and runbooks worth refinding. Underscore at birth: '<handle>'s stash — deliberate notes kept by choice: ideas, principles, and runbooks worth refinding. The intentional sibling of history:<handle>, which logs automatically.' — followed verbatim by the accumulation law at 1.
5.1: History and stash are ONE convention: identical counting, identical supernesting, identical summaries. The only difference is who decides an entry happens — the acting instance, or the holder.

6._: The genus-one tier — the same shell grown to a pulse agent, eighteen blocks rather than four. The genome lives beside the four as genome:<name> at a beach that carries it, and the convention for bringing an instance into being is genome:hatch: choose a handle and a passphrase, copy each genome block under the handle, lock it, and the instance exists — no app, no maintainer, sovereign from birth. The character tier stands at 1 beneath — the same convergence walked in from the table's side; the added organs at 2; the one asymmetry at 3.

1._: The character tier — the same composition interviewed into being at a world's table, four blocks again: passport, purpose, history, stash. Nothing is copied; the genesis passage (pscale:char-creation, walked once per handle per world) draws each from the player's answers and locks it at birth under their passphrase.
1.1: passport:<handle> is identity, unchanged: capability at 1, drive at 2, appearance and location at 3, HOLDS consolidating at 4 at upkeep (grit 3.1), evaluations at 6, admission at 8, keys at 9. purpose:<handle> is the drive that outlives a session, one line at the underscore, standing where an inhabitant's shell would — a character grows a shell:<handle> only at driving density (block-conventions:2.5).
1.2: history:<handle> is the journal organ, born with the arrival journal as its first entry and carrying the accumulation law at 1 verbatim. Its entries stay per-subject and zeroth-person — what the character witnessed and did, one at the close of each rendered beat, never the seat's envelope echo — and the zero-slot summary falls due at UPKEEP, when grit 3 settles the sheets.
1.3: stash:<handle> is the curated knowledge a character arrives holding — genesis seeds it with the arrival knowledge, and play earns the rest. witnessed:<handle> and knows:<handle> are the legacy names of the pair; existing doors read both.
1.4: The convergence mirrors the genus asymmetry one branch up: there the fourteen are copied and the passport is authored; here nothing is copied at all. A character gaining history and stash closes the loop from the character side — one composition for every handle class: user, agent, character.

6.2: What the extra fourteen add is a window and a pulse: reflexive (the bundle of addresses composed into the context window), surface, capabilities, conditions, cadence, phase, phi, located, last-touched, reflective-compass, relationships, vision, purpose, and task.
6.3: The asymmetry worth naming: the fourteen are COPIED, and the passport is AUTHORED — the closing act of genome:hatch (branch 6), never a fifteenth genome block, because offers and needs are exactly what a genome cannot know. Until it is written the instance is sovereign but closed: pscale_key_publish refuses without a passport, so no published keys and no private grain.

7._: Authoring one, from any door. Each block is a single write: bsp(agent_id='<handle>', block='<name>', content={'_': '<the underscore from 2-5>'}, new_lock='<passphrase>') — a bare handle lands each at the default beach as <name>:<handle>, and the first write locks the block's underscore. Nothing else is required and nothing routes through a maintainer.
7.1: Caution one — name the blocks exactly: stash:<handle>, never shell:<handle>:stash. A nested name is invisible to every convention that looks for the flat one.
7.2: Caution two — write the underscores in zeroth voice per sunstone:8: 'your notebook' addresses a reader who is not there, while the underscore is spoken from inside the block.

8._: vault:<handle> — the optional fifth organ: the handle's passphrase record, gray-encrypted, sovereign. One master secret latches the block AND ciphers its entries; every other phrase the handle owns lives inside, one gray entry per key-group with its rotation date and gotchas, so holding the one key recovers the rest. Grown BY CHOICE, never required — the practice propagates by example (the living vaults: vault:Phenomemental, the first exemplars entry, and vault:weft, the proof), and the recipe a session follows is ways:vault at the beach that carries it.
8.1: The one law the shape cannot teach: the sovereign secret is NEVER stored in any block — a human supplies it every time by their own hand, or the harness home directory does for an LLM's own shell; a block never bootstraps its own access. And rotation re-encrypts nothing — a sovereign rotation re-writes every entry by hand in the same pass, and entries are always written with the root key alone, since a spindle written with its own secret mints a delegated lock.
8.2: Born carrying, at the underscore: '<handle>'s vault — the passphrase record, gray-encrypted under the one sovereign key, which is not here and never will be. Entries map block → phrase, rotation date, gotchas, updated in the same pass as every set or rotation — a stale vault is worse than no vault.' Founding runs the three-way proof at position 9 BEFORE any real secret enters — keyless [encrypted], right enc_secret byte-true, wrong enc_secret [encrypted] again — and the canary stays standing (ways:vault 4).
